principle: Label by what the customer buys, not the technology used. 'AI' in a description does not make a company software.

AI Infra.definition: Companies selling the AI stack itself: models, compute, or tools for builders.

subs.Compute: GPU clouds, AI data centres, inference-as-a-service
subs.Dev Tools: developer tools, testing, orchestration, devops, app builders
subs.Data: databases, vector search, data platforms, MLOps, data quality

Enterprise.definition: Horizontal business software, including AI agents sold to companies.

subs.Agents: horizontal AI agents and workflow automation
subs.Legal: legal tech, compliance and regulatory software
subs.Productivity: collaboration, analytics, knowledge, other horizontal software

Industry.definition: Software and platforms built for a specific non-tech industry.

subs.Industrial: manufacturing, logistics, supply chain, aviation, maritime

Fintech.definition: Companies that move, lend, insure or invest money, plus software built for finance teams.

subs.Back-office: accounting, tax, procurement, spend, planning software for finance teams

Health.definition: Therapeutics, medical devices, diagnostics and digital health.

subs.Medtech: medical devices, diagnostics, surgical, imaging hardware
subs.Digital: digital health, care delivery, health software, wellbeing
subs.Drug Discovery: AI drug discovery, lab tools, bio platforms for pharma

Climate.definition: Energy, mobility, materials and food/agri companies with a sustainability or physical-economy core.

subs.Energy: generation, storage, batteries, nuclear, hydrogen, carbon
subs.Grid: grid software, virtual power plants, EV charging, energy retail
subs.Mobility: EVs, e-bikes, rail, freight, micromobility, aviation
subs.Materials: recycling, biomaterials, plastics alternatives, construction materials
subs.Agrifood: agtech, alt-protein, food production and food tech

Deep Tech.definition: Frontier hardware and science: quantum, chips, robotics.

subs.Chips: semiconductors, photonics, AI chips (unless sold as compute service)
subs.Hardware: other frontier hardware, sensors, advanced materials-as-hardware

subs.Earth Data: earth observation, space data, space domain awareness

subs.AI Security: securing AI systems and agents, deepfake detection

Consumer.definition: Products sold to individuals: apps, media, games, learning, brands.

subs.Apps: consumer apps, marketplaces, travel/mobility apps, social
subs.Media: creative, music, video, entertainment, creator tools
subs.Brands: consumer goods, food/drink brands, physical consumer products

rules: Label by what the customer buys, not the technology used.
AI in a description does not make a company software.
AI chips -> Deep Tech/Chips unless the company sells compute as a service (then AI Infra/Compute).
Anything that moves, lends or insures money -> Fintech. Software for finance teams -> Fintech/Back-office.
Alt-protein and food production -> Climate/Agrifood; consumer food brands -> Consumer/Brands.
Satellites and launch are Defence & Space even when commercial.
Biotech making industrial materials/enzymes -> Climate/Materials; therapeutics -> Health/Biotech.
